records.report:
In the medial compartment, there is radial tear at the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. There is displaced meniscal fragment into the medial gutter. There is focal subchondral bone sclerosis combining with extensive marrow edema at weightbaring medial femoral condyle (about 1.6*2.3 cm). 
  
 The lateral compartment, the lateral meniscus is not torn. The articular cartilage appears normal.  
  
 The patellofemoral joint, there is diffuse low grade and high grade chondrosis (less than and more than 50% thickness cartilage loss) along medial, lateral patellar facets, medial and lateral trochleas. The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
  
 In the intercondylar notch, the anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are intact. There is no tibial translation. 
  
 The medial collateral ligament complexes are intact. The posteromedial oblique ligament is intact.  
  
 The lateral collateral ligament complexes are intact. The popliteofibular ligament is intact. The meniscopopliteal fascicles are intact.  
  
 The extensor mechanism is normal.  
  
 Large amount of left knee effusion with synovitis is present. The surrounding musculature is normal.   Patellofemoral compartmental osteoarthritis of left knee by evidence of chondrosis and osteophytes. 
  Focal subchondral bone sclerosis (early insufficiency fracture) combining with extensive marrow edema at weightbaring medial femoral condyle (about 1.6*2.3 cm). 
  Radial tear at the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. (note: meniscal extrusion into the medial gutter). 
  Large amount of left knee effusion with synovitis.
